fit: date fruit at iftar in interviews of adults with diabetes
assessment: Two Riyadh groups describe the ceremonial practice and differences in amounts. There are no date-attributable pain measurements or Parkinson population.

fit: fasting and medication adjustments in a Parkinson cohort
assessment: The authors analyzed 20 of 24 people and report an unchanged nonmotor total. The foods at iftar and pain items are unreported. Treat MDS abstract 1106 as a probable same-cohort report.

fit: qualitative iftar fruit routine and a separate meal-size and discomfort account
assessment: One participant mentions dates and water. Another attributed less hunger discomfort to smaller portions. The observations do not form an ingredient comparison and the cohort is not Parkinson-specific.

fit: medication and aggregate nonmotor scores during Ramadan in Parkinson disease
assessment: Seventy-five fasting participants self-selected medication groups. Table 2 reports overall questionnaire totals but no pain item or fruit exposure.

fit: Kuwait Parkinson cohort, nonmotor totals during a fasting and medication context
assessment: Nonmotor scores were unchanged in the 20-person completer comparison. The report does not identify constituent food intake or a separate apathy result.

fit: self-selected medication and nonmotor totals during Ramadan in Parkinson disease
assessment: The average total was lower in the adapted medication group and higher in the comparator by follow-up. Individual apathy outcomes and date exposure were not reported.
